_meta.source: WebSearch pass across r/weightroom, r/Fitness, r/powerlifting context, strongerbyscience.com, strengthlog.com, science-in-sport, 2026-dated fitness press
_meta.purpose: Trending lifter-facing questions to layer on top of the 28 PubMed-anchored themes in keyword_research_2026-04-13.json. Each topic here must be paired with one or more verified PubMed papers from the research file (or a fresh verified search) before entering the draft pipeline — topics alone are NOT drafting fodder.
_meta.pairing_rule: For every trending topic below, the drafter must attach >= 1 citation whose DOI has been PubMed-verified. No topic draft may ship until the F-0 gate passes.

trending_topics.question: Is recovery the real limiter on my gains, not effort?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: 2026 fitness press frames recovery as the primary limiter, shifting away from 'hardcore = overtraining' culture. Reddit threads echo 'why am I not recovering enough' as a top intermediate question.
trending_topics.draft_angle: Recovery is programming, not a rest day. Sleep, protein, deload weeks, and RPE tracking are the levers.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: resistance training recovery monitoring fatigue deload systematic review

trending_topics.question: Does it matter if I train each muscle 2x/week vs 4x/week if total volume is the same?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: Stronger by Science and Weightology both cover this as one of the most-asked hypertrophy questions. Reddit form-check culture treats high-frequency as superior; research shows near-equivalence when volume is matched.
trending_topics.draft_angle: When weekly set volume is matched, frequency effects on hypertrophy are negligible. Train at the frequency you recover from.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: training frequency hypertrophy meta-analysis equated volume

trending_topics.question: Is more volume always better, or is there a point where it starts hurting gains?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: The 'J-shaped' dose-response curve is a current Stronger-by-Science talking point. 10-15 sets/muscle/week is the new consensus floor, but 'how high before it backfires' is the actual question lifters ask.
trending_topics.draft_angle: More volume helps until it doesn't — the J-shaped response. 10-15 sets/muscle/week is a good floor; past ~20 sets gains flatten and recovery cost rises.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: resistance training volume dose response hypertrophy

trending_topics.question: Should I take creatine before or after lifting — does it actually matter?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: 2022 meta + newer Nutrition reviews suggest post-workout + carb/protein is slightly better. One of the most-searched supplement timing questions in 2026.
trending_topics.draft_angle: For strength/hypertrophy, post-workout creatine shows a small edge over pre-workout, but daily consistency matters far more than the time of day.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: creatine timing pre post exercise resistance training

trending_topics.question: Is there really an anabolic window? Do I need to slam protein within 30 min of lifting?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: Protein timing is still one of the top Reddit/Google questions despite the evidence being settled. The 'window' has widened from '30 min' to 'within a few hours'.
trending_topics.draft_angle: The anabolic window is 2-3 hours wide, not 30 minutes. Total daily protein dominates; timing is a minor lever.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: protein timing muscle protein synthesis anabolic window meta-analysis

trending_topics.question: My squat looks different from the coaching cue videos — am I doing it wrong?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: Squat/deadlift form-check is 98% of r/Fitness form-check posts per multiple aggregators. Most 'wrong' squats are anthropometric variance, not form errors.
trending_topics.draft_angle: Squat shape varies with femur:torso ratio. More forward lean is not a form error — it's anatomy. Chase neutral spine + full depth, not someone else's camera angle.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: squat biomechanics anthropometry individual variance kinematics

trending_topics.question: What is the minimum effective warmup before heavy lifting?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: Stronger by Science piece 'Your Warm-up Doesn't Need to Be That Complicated' + Military.com 'Mobility 20/20'. Lifters ask 'can I skip mobility and just ramp up weight?'
trending_topics.draft_angle: 5 min light cardio + dynamic movement + progressive warmup sets covers the evidence base. Static stretches >30s reduce power output — skip them pre-lift.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: warmup static stretching power output 1RM strength meta-analysis

trending_topics.question: Is static stretching before lifting bad for you?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: Consistent current answer across science-in-sport and strongerbyscience is 'yes, for the session'. 2026 press continues to rebuff this.
trending_topics.draft_angle: Long static holds before a session reduce force output and power for that session. Do them after, not before.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: static stretching acute effect force power resistance exercise

trending_topics.question: Why does the same training volume wreck me at 42 when it was fine at 25?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: Sullivan/Baker 'Volume and the Masters Lifter' is a long-running reference. 40+ recovery capacity and volume tolerance is a top question for returning lifters.
trending_topics.draft_angle: Recovery capacity drops with age, not peak strength. 40+ lifters need more rest days, lower peak volume, but the same intensity can be kept. Train smarter with more frequency variation.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: masters lifters resistance training age recovery volume

trending_topics.question: Will heavy lifting make me bulky as a woman?
trending_topics.why_it_trends: The #1 most-searched women's lifting myth in 2026 press. Still getting asked despite being settled for a decade.
trending_topics.draft_angle: Testosterone levels 15-20x lower than men cap hypertrophy. Heavy lifting builds strength and bone density, not a bodybuilder physique. 'Toned' = lifting + body comp management, not light weights.
trending_topics.pubmed_search_backup: women resistance training hypertrophy testosterone strength
